messages:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a regression with Python SDK tool/function calling + structured output. After updating to 0.23.1, our function calls started raising SchemaValidationError for responses that used to be accepted. Likely related to the stricter type coercion added recently.

jon: Can you paste a minimal repro? Is this with fn.call() or tool.call()?

maria: fn.call(), calling a user-registered function that expects a typed dataclass. Previously the runtime coalesced numbers/strings for simple fields. Now we get: `SchemaValidationError: expected int but got str` even though model returned "42".

maria: Minimal snippet:
```python
from redwood import Client
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass
class Order:
    id: int
    note: str

client = Client()
res = client.fn.call("create_order", input={"id": "42", "note": "fast"})
print(res)
```

sam: Reproduced locally on 0.23.1. 0.22.6 accepts "42" and coerces to int. Regression introduced by strict schema checking PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/512).

elaine: That PR was intended to avoid undefined behavior with nested schemas. But we didn't intend to break simple primitive coercion. Good catch.

jon: Two questions: 1) Should SDK keep implicit coercion for primitive types? 2) If so, how to scope it (global flag, per-call option, or follow model-provided content-type hints)?

leo: My vote: opt-in flag per call eg `coerce_primitives=True` so we don't change default behavior suddenly. Then we can flip default in a major version after bake-in.

maria: That would unblock us quickly. Could we also add a diagnostic field in the error that includes the raw returned token span so we can patch prompts? Right now we lose context.

sam: +1 for diagnostic info. PR #520 (WIP) adds `RawResponse` to exception.metadata. Will push tests today.

dev-bot: CI pipeline started for branch feature/primitive-coercion (build 3492).

jon: Implementation note: coercion is straightforward for builtin types (int/float/bool) but breakpoints around `null` and empty strings. We should specify exact coercion rules in docs and tests. Also consider locale for floats (`,` vs `.`) — probably ignore.

elaine: Agreed. Also add a compatibility test that runs previous SDK fixtures producing string numbers. We'll add a matrix: strict vs coercion.

maria: For UX, can we make the exception message actionable: include `expected_type`, `actual_value`, `suggested_fix` (e.g., `wrap in int(...) or enable coerce_primitives`). That will save support tickets.

leo: On the async side, note that `client.afn.call` already had slightly different error surface — need to parallelize the change. I can take the async path.

sam: I'll own the sync implementation and tests. Planning to open PR with setting `coerce_primitives=False` default and a per-call arg. Link to issue: #788 (SDK: toolcall primitive coercion).

jon: One more thing — telemetry. If we enable coercion per-call, we should emit an opt-in metric so we can measure how many orgs rely on it before considering default change. Add `telemetry.coercion_used` signal. Keep it privacy-safe (no value content).

maria: Sounds great. ETA for a patch?

sam: I'll have a draft PR by EOD PT. Tests + docs tomorrow.

elaine: I'll coordinate a short changelog blurb and a migration note.

maria: Thanks all. This unblocks our staging tests. Please ping if you need a sample dataset.

leo: PRs: sync (#521), async (#522). Assigning reviews to @jon and @elaine.

dev-bot: build 3492 failed on lint (flake8): `sdk/python/redwood/clients/schema_coerce.py: line 72: E203`

sam: fixing lint now.

maria: Appreciate the quick turnaround! :rocket:
